fw.intro: Job families and roles, competencies and versioned qualification standards. Revising a standard creates a new version and flags affected records for review.
fw.regulatedEdit: Regulated role ({ref}): entry requirements follow the regulation and are not edited here.
fw.reasonHint: Saving creates a new role version; the change is recorded in the audit log.
fw.standardsIntro: Standards are versioned. Only the current version is used for new qualifications; superseded versions stay for history. Task lists are edited in the standard editor.
fw.reviseBody: A new version takes effect today. The current version becomes superseded and every active qualification against it is flagged for review.

nexus.notAuthority: Kafa'a mirrors who decides; it never decides or changes the authority matrix. Licensing decisions stay with FANR, employment decisions with ENEC and Nawah.
nexus.mSkippedSub: Kafa'a-only personas have no NEXUS profile

quals.title: Qualification outcomes
quals.body: NEXUS talent views receive qualification outcomes (qualified, due, expired), never the underlying records.

catalogue.title: One learning catalogue
catalogue.body: Training programmes and courses in NEXUS and Kafa'a should be one catalogue; the owner is still to be agreed.

readiness.title: Supplier readiness hand-off
readiness.body: When a supplier is ready to register, Kafa'a hands off to the NEXUS partner readiness lens.

partners.title: Shared organisation records
partners.body: The partners directory reads shared organisation and partnership records instead of keeping its own copy.

identity.title: Identity and language

nexus.noLedgerBody: Material actions such as sign-offs, role grants and access reviews appear here.

audit.intro: Every write and every refusal, in order. Entries are hash-chained and cannot be edited or deleted.
audit.appendOnly: Append-only: the database rejects any change or deletion of an audit entry, and this console has no edit or delete control.
audit.noEdit: Audit entries cannot be changed. To correct a record, make a new entry through the normal workflow.

ai.intro: How every recommendation in Kafa'a works, what it never uses, whether its outcomes are fair across groups, and every change to its settings. All engines are deterministic and explain each result; no model is connected.
ai.footerTitle: What this page is, and is not
ai.footerBody: A governance view of Kafa'a's own suggestion engines on a synthetic demo population. It makes no decision about anyone: suggestions inform people and managers, and HR and line managers decide. A flag starts a review; it does not change anyone's results.

stat.cardsSub: {n} can be switched off by each person
stat.protectedSub: Gender, nationality and age: checked by an automated test on every build
stat.optouts: Opted out of the Learning Coach
stat.optoutsSub: People who switched ranked suggestions off

cards.intro: One card per surface that ranks or scores. Weights are live from the engine settings; a change to them gives every card on that engine a new version.

card.neverTested: No scoring function reads these fields: checked by an automated test on every build.
card.optOutYes: Each person can switch it off
card.functions: For auditors: the {n} functions behind this card

metricHelp.navigator_ready: Share of staff with at least one role within two steps rated "ready now" or "ready within 3 years" (people who switched the Navigator off are left out).
metricHelp.opportunity_selected: Share of applicants selected for (or who completed) at least one opportunity.
metricHelp.mentoring_matched: Share of people who asked for mentoring and were matched.
metricHelp.hipo_pool: Share of staff in the high-potential pool (talent review placements when present, else the leadership pipeline the pool feeds).

fair.howBody: Each week Kafa'a compares outcome rates between women and men, and between Emirati and other nationalities. A group whose rate is below {pct}% of the best group's rate is flagged (the four-fifths rule). If any group has fewer than 10 people the whole comparison is suppressed, so no small group can be worked out by subtraction. People with no recorded value are left out of that comparison.
fair.noneBody: Run the weekly snapshot to compare outcomes across groups.
fair.resultsDesc: Outcomes as of {date}. Bars show each group's rate; the line marks four-fifths of the best rate.
fair.suppressedBody: A group has fewer than 10 people, so this comparison is not shown (no counts, no rates, no flag).
fair.trendTitle: Lowest group ratio per metric, by week
fair.trendBody: The lowest group rate as a percentage of the best group's rate (shown comparisons only). Below the dashed line is a flag.
fair.flagBody: AI governance and HR review the engine card, the inputs and the human decisions behind the outcome within two weeks, and record what they found in the change log if weights change. No individual result is changed by the monitor, and the flag alone is not evidence of discrimination.
fair.confirmBody: Kafa'a recomputes this week's outcome rates for every group, replaces this week's rows and records the run in the audit log and the NEXUS ledger.

log.intro: Every change to an engine or its weights, with before and after, the rationale, and its audit and NEXUS ledger entries.
log.noRationale: No rationale (switched from the integrations card)

weights.noModel: No model gateway is configured, so the deterministic engine keeps serving and the surface shows "model unavailable".
weights.title: Weights (0 to 10)
weights.none: This engine has no adjustable weights.
weights.range: Each weight must be a number from 0 to 10.
weights.rationaleHint: At least {n} characters: why the change, and what evidence supports it.
weights.confirmBody: The new settings apply at once to every surface on this engine. Each card on it gets a new version, and the change is written to the change log, the audit log and the NEXUS ledger.

opt.title: Opt-outs by surface
opt.body: People who switched ranked suggestions off. Each person decides on their settings page; nobody else sees who.
opt.requestsHidden: Visible to platform admins and auditors.
opt.requestsNote: Handled through the data rights queue with the same 30-day target as every other request.

optedOut.title: You switched off {surface} suggestions

body.coach: No ranked learning cards are shown. Here is the full staff catalogue in plain order; your mandatory training is still assigned as usual.
body.navigator: No readiness ranking is shown. Here are the published roles by job family; the career paths show every route.
body.marketplace: No match scores or top picks are shown. Opportunities are listed by start date.

optedOut.note: You can switch it back on at any time.

unranked.catalogueBody: All staff courses by code. Nothing here is ranked for you.
unranked.rolesBody: Every published role, alphabetical. Nothing here is rated for you.

settings.title: Recommendations and your data
settings.intro: Kafa'a's suggestions come from deterministic engines that explain every result. They never use your gender, nationality or age. You can switch ranked suggestions off on each surface below; the full lists stay available.

offBody.navigator: You see the roles and career paths without a readiness ranking.
offBody.coach: You see the course catalogue in plain order instead of ranked learning cards.
offBody.marketplace: You see opportunities by start date, without match scores.

settings.othersBody: These suggest only when you ask (mentors, rotations, experts, Future Me) or support a human decision (talent review). They have no personal switch; you can read how each works and ask for a correction.
settings.export: Download what Kafa'a infers about me (JSON)
settings.never: Your choices are recorded in the audit log and the NEXUS ledger. HR and admins see only how many people switched a surface off, never who.

consequenceOff.navigator: The Career Navigator stops rating your readiness for roles and shows the roles and paths in plain order instead.
consequenceOff.coach: The Learning Coach stops ranking learning for you and shows the course catalogue in plain order. Mandatory training is still assigned.
consequenceOff.marketplace: The marketplace stops scoring opportunities for you and lists them by start date. You can still apply to any opportunity.

settings.consequenceOn: Ranked suggestions with their reasons come back on this surface.

export.done: Your AI inferences file is downloaded
export.failed: The file could not be prepared. Try again.
export.logged: Self-service export: what Kafa'a infers about me (AI inferences)

correct.title: Ask for a correction
correct.intro: Tell us which inference looks wrong, for example a skill level, a piece of evidence or a readiness rating. A person reviews it; nothing changes automatically.
correct.hint: Name the skill, record or role, and what you believe is right.
correct.sla: Answered within 30 days through the data rights process, like every other request.

kindHelp.add: a new skill that is developed and assessed on its own
kindHelp.rename: a clearer name; the old one stays as an alternative label
kindHelp.split: one skill becomes two to four; the original is kept as obsolete
kindHelp.retire: mark obsolete with a replacement; never removed
kindHelp.relevel: change the key level or its level essence

incHelp.skill: A change targets a live skill; an addition targets none.
incHelp.names: Both names are given (up to 120 characters); a split names every part.
incHelp.distinct_name: No other live skill uses the name or an alternative label, and the parts differ from each other.
incHelp.development: Say how the skill is developed, separately from other skills (20 characters or more).
incHelp.assessment: Say how the skill is assessed, separately from other skills (20 characters or more).
incHelp.source: A new skill cites a public https source.
incHelp.replacement: A replacement, if named, is another live skill.
incHelp.level: A new skill has a key level from one to four, a competency and an area; a re-level changes the level or its essence.

msg.not_signed_in: Sign in to propose or decide a skill change.
msg.forbidden_propose: Only staff may propose a change to the skills catalogue.
msg.forbidden_decide: Only skills council members (training manager, HR director, platform admin) decide skill changes.
msg.kind: Choose add, rename, split, retire or re-level.
msg.rationale: Give a rationale of 10 to 1,000 characters: the council reads it before deciding.
msg.not_found: That skill or request does not exist.
msg.duplicate: An open request already covers this skill: comment on it instead of opening a second one.
msg.inclusion: The proposal does not meet the inclusion rule yet: see the checks.
msg.own_request: Maker-checker: you proposed this change, so two other council members decide it.
msg.second_approver: Maker-checker: you already voted on this request; a different council member gives the second decision.
msg.note: Give the reason for a rejection (10 to 500 characters): it is shown to the proposer.
msg.stale: The catalogue changed since this request was made: it no longer applies as written.
msg.forbidden_queue: Only skills council members and auditors see the council queue.

log.intro: The public log of the skills catalogue. A skills council of operations, engineering, training and HR representatives decides every change; two different members approve it, and retired skills stay readable as obsolete.

how.inclusion: Inclusion rule: a skill is in the catalogue only when it is developed and assessed distinctly from every other skill, with distinct names and a public source.
how.council: Maker-checker: two different council members decide each change, neither of them the proposer, and every vote is written to the evidence ledger.
how.obsolete: Obsolete, never removed: a retired skill keeps its page, history and evidence, and points to its replacement.
how.methodology: A change that moves counts or levels carries a methodology banner on the dashboards it affects for the next ninety days.

log.srcUpkeep: Jobs and Skills Australia · Australian Skills Classification (retired for timeliness)
log.proposeHint: Staff can propose a change after signing in.

prop.intro: Propose a change to the skills catalogue. The inclusion rule is checked as you type; the skills council then decides, with two members who are not you.
prop.essenceHint: Left empty, the generic essence of the new level is used.
prop.developmentHint: The course, practice or route that builds this skill and not another ({n} characters or more).
prop.assessmentHint: The assessment that shows this skill and not another ({n} characters or more).
prop.rationaleHint: The council reads this before deciding.
prop.ready: Ready: the inclusion rule is met.
prop.checkBody: Checked live with the same rule the council and both backends use.

effect.add: If published: a new skill at version 1, with a review date one review cycle away. It starts as an orphan until a course, assessment or role uses it.
effect.rename: If published: the new name, the old name kept as an alternative label, the version raised by one and the review clock restarted.
effect.split: If published: the new skills are added and the original is marked obsolete, replaced by the first part. Nothing is removed.
effect.retire: If published: the skill is marked obsolete with today's date and its replacement. It stays readable with its history; nothing is removed.
effect.relevel: If published: the new key level and essence, the version raised by one and the review clock restarted. Dashboards show a methodology banner.

prop.councilBody: Two different skills council members (training manager, HR director or platform admin), neither of them you. Each vote is ledgered; a disagreement sends the request back.
prop.confirmTitle: Send this proposal to the skills council?
prop.confirmBody: "{title}" goes to the council queue. You can follow it below; the council decides with two members.
prop.sent: Change request sent to the skills council
prop.mineNone: You have not proposed a change yet.
prop.mineNoneBody: Proposals you send appear here with the council's votes.
prop.waiting: Waiting for the first council vote.
prop.seeLog: See it in the change log

cn.intro: The skills council decides every change to the skills catalogue. Two different members, neither of them the proposer, each record a vote; agreement closes the request and a published change is applied and logged publicly.
cn.noAccess: The council queue is open to skills council members and auditors.
cn.readOnly: You can read the queue and every vote. Only council members (training manager, HR director, platform admin) vote.

rules.two: Two different members decide each change: the first vote approves or rejects, a second member who agrees closes it.
rules.proposer: The proposer never votes on their own request, and nobody votes twice.
rules.ledger: Every vote is confirmed, audited and written to the NEXUS evidence ledger.
rules.obsolete: Retired and split skills are marked obsolete with a replacement; nothing is removed from the catalogue.
rules.banner: A change that moves counts or levels shows a methodology banner on the affected dashboards for ninety days.

cn.planObsolete: The current skill is marked obsolete and keeps its history.
cn.planBanner: Affected dashboards show a methodology banner.
cn.secondHint: A member has {decision}; your vote decides if you agree.

consequence.first: This is the first council vote. A different member must agree before anything changes in the catalogue.
consequence.final: This is the second, agreeing vote: it closes the request. An approval applies the change to the catalogue and publishes it in the change log.
consequence.differ: Your vote differs from the first one: the request goes back to the queue for a fresh first vote.

cn.noteRequired: Reason for the rejection (shown to the proposer)

done.differ: Votes differ: the request is back in the queue

hl.intro: How current the catalogue is: definitions past their review date, and live skills that nothing teaches, assesses or uses. Every number opens its list of skills.

cover.taughtRole: Taught and used by a role
cover.roleOnly: Used by a role, not taught

hl.coverNote: {n} of {total} live skills are taught by a course, pathway or external resource, or assessed.
hl.taughtTitle: What counts as taught or used

taught.course: A catalogue course (supplier-academy courses excluded) that teaches the skill: it names the skill in its evidence keys, holds the competency of a core skill, or has an active course link. Security skills are never taught here.
taught.pathway: A published pathway for the skill whose learning step is filled.
taught.external: A published external resource from the curated catalogue that names the skill.
taught.assessment: A current qualification standard, an adaptive bank or item, a performance task, a twin or AI drill, or a fitness-check area that assesses the skill.
taught.role: A published role profile that requires the skill (career-path-only roles excluded).

hl.taughtShared: Courses, pathways and external resources follow the exact rule of the curriculum coverage scorer, so both pages agree on what the catalogue teaches.
hl.whyBody: Skills catalogues go stale when no one owns their upkeep. Each skill has an owner and a review cycle by how fast it changes; an orphaned skill is a candidate to retire or to connect to a course, assessment or role.

mb.title: The skills catalogue changed on {date} ({n} methodology changes in the window)
mb.body: Counts and levels on this page may move compared with earlier periods. Kinds of change in the last {days} days: {kinds}.

ds.intro: A datasheet for the skills ontology: what is in it, where it comes from, how often it changes, which languages it covers, how skill inference works and how bias is handled. Every figure is computed from the catalogue when the page opens.
ds.generated: Generated {date} from the live catalogue · last published change {last}

tile.bilingualSub: names and definitions in English and Arabic

size.title: Size and scope
size.body: {skills} skills, {live} of them live, each with one of {owners} owners responsible for its upkeep.

sources.title: Sources

cadence.title: Update cadence
cadence.body: Each skill is reviewed on a cycle set by how fast it changes: every {fast} months for fast-changing skills, {standard} for standard and {slow} for slow-changing ones.
cadence.kinds: Published in a year by kind: {list}.

lang.title: Languages
lang.body: English and Arabic are both first-class: every field below is counted separately in each language.

inf.title: How inference works
inf.body: A skill level is inferred only from evidence: {kinds} evidence kinds on {bases} bases, each decaying with a half-life of {fast}, {standard} or {slow} months by how fast the skill changes.
inf.surfaces: {n} places rank options for people ({first} from the first transparency wave and {added} added since), each with a published engine card.
inf.deterministic: {n} of them run a deterministic, explainable engine; {model} server-side model slots are enabled.
inf.claims: A self-assessment or manager rating never raises a verified level on its own; verified evidence always wins.

bias.title: How bias is handled
bias.body: {protected} protected attributes are never an input to any engine. Fairness is measured by group with a minimum group of {min} and the four-fifths rule ({pct} percent).
bias.metrics: {n} fairness outcomes are measured each week.
bias.without: {n} ranked surfaces have no outcome to compare (content ranking, anonymous use or no recorded outcome); their engine cards say why.
bias.suppress: Any group under {min} people suppresses the whole comparison, so no small group can be singled out.

limits.title: Limits of this datasheet
limits.synthetic: The people, evidence and outcomes behind these figures are synthetic demonstration data.
limits.mirror: Licensing and qualification facts mirror NEXUS; this catalogue does not decide any licence.
limits.claims: The datasheet describes the platform; it is not a certification or a regulatory statement.
limits.security: Security-sensitive skills are described at a general level only.

reg.howBody: Any place that ranks courses, people, roles or options for a person is listed here with its engine card: what it uses, what it never uses, the functions that score it, and the outcome checked for fairness. An automated check fails the build if a new ranking appears without a card.
reg.defaultsNote: Transform and assess surfaces have no admin switch: they always run their deterministic default, so they are carded but cannot be turned off.

kernelNote.transform: Transform runs its deterministic default only; it has no admin switch.
kernelNote.assess: Assess runs its deterministic default only; it has no admin switch.
kernelNote.rules: A fixed rule set: the same inputs always give the same order.

metricHelp.digest_suggested: Share of staff for whom the weekly digest suggested at least one item.
metricHelp.career_mode_used: Share of staff who used Dalil in career mode.
metricHelp.pathway_enrolled: Share of staff enrolled in a pathway the engine suggested.
metricHelp.external_completed: Share of staff who completed a ranked external course.
metricHelp.fitness_completed: Share of staff who completed a suggested fitness drill.
metricHelp.gig_selected: Share of staff selected for a future-skills gig.
metricHelp.twin_passed: Share of staff who passed a suggested digital-twin drill.
metricHelp.adaptive_completed: Share of staff who completed an adaptive lesson.
metricHelp.instructor_nominated: Share of eligible staff nominated as instructors.

none.f24: Measured in the first-wave fairness tab
none.content: Ranks content, not people: no group outcome
none.anonymous: Used anonymously: no group data is kept
none.no_outcome: No recorded outcome to compare yet
none.non_staff: Serves applicants or students, not staff

sf.howTitle: Fairness of the newer ranked surfaces
sf.howBody: Each week the outcome of every newer ranked surface is compared by gender and nationality. A group under ten people suppresses the whole comparison; a group whose rate is under {pct} percent of the best group is flagged for review.
sf.confirmTitle: Run the surface fairness snapshot for {period}?
sf.confirmBody: Recomputes this week's comparisons from current outcomes and replaces this week's rows. Audited and written to the ledger.
